video_title: Stop planning for 2027: how OpenAI builds product 90 days at a time | Tara Sesha and Nan Yu (OpenAI)
gist: OpenAI product leaders Tara Sesha and Nan Yu explain planning AI products on a 2-3 month horizon, shipping imperfect features fast, handling enterprise absorption limits, agent design, and predictions for voice, proactive agents and hardware in 2027.

insights.claim: OpenAI product leader Tara Sesha says the right planning horizon for AI products is about two to three months out: far enough to anticipate model capability, short enough to avoid wrong multi-year predictions.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Annual 2027 roadmaps for AI-native products are likely to be wrong; shorter cycles are the edge.
insights.quote: it's like two to three months out

insights.claim: Tara Sesha keeps a personal document of incorrectly predicted AI developments to remind herself she cannot predict years out, yet argues building only for today gets a product left behind.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Both over-anchoring on the present and over-futurism are failure modes.

insights.claim: Planning horizon should depend on market dynamics: Stripe's payments market can be modeled with bull/base/bear cases and annual planning, whereas OpenAI's business cannot be forecast that way.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Stable-structure businesses keep long plans; AI model-driven businesses cannot.

insights.claim: OpenAI's internal ship bar for a product is whether it aims at where models will be in two to three months, is not overly anchored in the present, and is not so futuristic as to be unusable.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Products timed to next-generation models capture value as capabilities arrive.

insights.claim: Tara Sesha, after about seven years at Stripe's polished culture, says urgency and empirical user feedback now outweigh a priori perfection when shipping AI products.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Speed of learning from real usage is the competitive variable in AI product development.
insights.quote: nothing compares to like the actual empirical evidence of seeing users try it, use it, and then iterating from there

insights.claim: OpenAI shipped an imperfect toggle to get an agentic harness to ChatGPT's billion-plus users without disrupting developer workflows, expecting the toggle to be removed in about a year.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Agent distribution via ChatGPT's user base is prioritized over UX elegance; expect UX simplification later.

insights.claim: OpenAI uses internal dogfooding as a quality gate: ship internally and look at retention, delight and novel model use cases; weak internal uptake signals a product should not ship.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Internal retention is a cheap leading indicator for external product-market fit.

insights.claim: Nan Yu says the biggest constraint on AI products is people's ability to absorb capability, since models can do far more than users take advantage of (capability overhang).
insights.speaker: Nan Yu (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Adoption, onboarding and education, not model quality, bound realized value.
insights.quote: people aren't necessarily taking advantage of all those abilities

insights.claim: OpenAI pushed agents onto enterprises that mostly used ChatGPT for Q&A, knowingly breaking their processes, because failing to ship frontier features risked customers switching to alternative products.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Enterprise AI vendors face leapfrog risk, so rapid change is accepted despite customer pain.
insights.quote: do what your users need, not what your users say they need

insights.claim: Nan Yu argues onboarding matters far more in the AI era because of capability overhang, and users need to understand initial experience and offering.
insights.speaker: Nan Yu (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Onboarding quality becomes a differentiator for AI products.

insights.claim: Tara Sesha says agent features that act semi-autonomously require users to understand privacy, data use and product norms so they can predict behavior, replacing reliance on settings menus.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Trust and predictability are product requirements for agents.

insights.claim: Nan Yu argues managing around 40 agents is unrealistic for human cognition; users in practice add a chief-of-staff agent, so agent products should bundle activity into a few managed groups.
insights.speaker: Nan Yu (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Hierarchical orchestrator agents are the likely dominant multi-agent UX.
insights.quote: you're not managing seven you're managing one

insights.claim: Tara Sesha says single versus multi-identity agent design depends on use-case specifics like data permissions, service-account versus user credentials, and segmented memory in private channels.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Agent architecture choices hinge on permissions and memory scoping, an enterprise-grade concern.

insights.claim: OpenAI's platform approach layers capabilities: native functionality, plugins and third-party hooks, then computer use as fallback, so a task can always be completed even without integrations.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Computer use is a universal fallback that reduces dependence on third-party integrations and consumes extra tokens.

insights.claim: Nan Yu says an agent that gets 99 percent of a job done then fails is worse than a non-starter, and computer use is valued because it reliably completes the job even if slow and token-costly.
insights.speaker: Nan Yu (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Reliability to completion beats elegance; computer use drives token consumption for model vendors.
insights.quote: the last mile honestly feels sometimes worse than just like it's a non-starter

insights.claim: Tara Sesha says working with research requires bringing specific user session examples and writing evals that show a prompt-and-skills outcome, which can then be post-trained into the model.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Product-written evals are the interface feeding user needs into model training.
insights.quote: writing evals as much as possible is like the most important thing

insights.claim: Tara Sesha predicts voice will be the major AI interface shift in 2027, citing GPT live, reduced family tech support, and ease onboarding OpenAI's people team.
insights.speaker: Tara Sesha (OpenAI)
insights.so_what: Voice interfaces gain share as models improve in speed and quality.
insights.quote: Voice I'm like so bullish on voice

insights.claim: Nan Yu predicts self-driving-like products that use themselves on the user's behalf will solve the empty-input-box problem and become standard within a year.
insights.speaker: Nan Yu (OpenAI)

insights.claim: Host Claire predicts hardware replacing the laptop, a small Codex-in-a-box device, will be a hot product in 2027.
insights.speaker: Claire (host)
insights.so_what: Signals interest in dedicated AI agent hardware.
